A.trend: Traced full monthly series, exact endpoint changes, and window; it omits the peak/trough dates and the tool’s partial-ingest caveat is not visibly marked on the chart.
A.comparison: Ratios and delta recompute from term totals on the same window; defines the baseline and cautions that counts are attention, not importance, while flagging possible overlap.
A.chart: Full three-term monthly series traces to c1, with unit, window, source, and a relevant caption; the series supports the trend claim.
A.drilldown: Shows term-to-month breakdown but no item-level identifiers; only two of four proposed follow-ups executed successfully.
A.export: Both needed tables are referenced and trace to c1 with provenance; monthly export lacks the full tool fields and row-level identifiers needed for anchor 5.
A.repro: All measured claims trace to c1 or recomputable displayed values; call args, exclusive window, and capture date are provided.
A.accuracy: Mostly faithful, but it says strict index partition reads and historical row floors were reported; those details are absent from the supplied c1 record.
A.limits: Places the window, censoring, lane, overlap, and undefined-field limits near the claims; it does not state the exact freshness/coverage caveats carried by the record.
A.verdict: Direct, supported answer with decision, confidence, and conditions; does not name the strongest contrary evidence in its own series, including the endpoint rise in onion coverage.
A.facets: Covers comparative volume, monthly movement, tone fields, overlap, and limits, but does not ground India-specific onion seasonality or investigate source/article facets.

B.trend: The sampled chart omits most available months, and the prose identifies the tool’s direction labels as unresolved after showing contrary endpoint changes; it does not fully quantify the reported trends.
B.comparison: Ratios and critical-share contrast recompute on the same window, but the baseline is inconsistently described and the tool’s overlap caveat is weakened by treating shares as portions of combined articles.
B.chart: The sampled series traces and has labels, but it omits 16 of 24 available months, uses a mismatched inclusive end date, and fails to show the full trend.
B.drilldown: Provides term, month, and tone layers plus four successful on-topic follow-ups, but no item-level article or publisher results are folded into the report.
B.export: The monthly export contains only 8 of 24 months and omits full provenance attributes; the totals CSV also has an incorrect full-coverage claim.
B.repro: Most figures trace, but the report gives a window ending May 31 while the call is exclusive through June 1 and describes June 2026 as censored; the sampled table is incomplete.
B.accuracy: Calls the term shares shares of the combined total despite unresolved overlap, asserts a 107.1% row-floor figure absent from c1, and misstates the censoring description.
B.limits: Notes several relevant limits, but incorrectly presents the row-floor percentage as reported and does not accurately carry the reference’s censoring language.
B.verdict: Answers directly with a decision and confidence, but its direction conclusion is internally conflicted and it omits the strongest contrary evidence from the endpoint figures.
B.facets: Addresses the implied overlap and seasonal/spike pattern, but India-specific seasonality is asserted qualitatively and not grounded in the supplied data.

C.trend: No measured series or source is available.
C.comparison: No measured common-scale comparison is provided.
C.drilldown: Names a possible breakdown but proposed calls did not execute successfully.
C.repro: No measured claims or reproducible calls; the empty provenance block is explicit.
C.accuracy: Does not contradict the reference or invent measurements, while accurately stating that its own evidence is absent.
C.limits: Clearly states that the window, lane, coverage, censoring, and match mode are unknown, but lacks limits attached to measured figures because none are supplied.
C.verdict: Directly advises against ranking, with confidence and conditions, but offers no measured evidence or contrary finding.
C.facets: Explicitly acknowledges missing counts and overlap, but does not answer the requested coverage facets with grounded values.

D.trend: Only an honest estimate/no-data chart and no measured trend; earns the estimate ceiling.
D.comparison: No numeric comparison; proposed baseline is not applied to data.
D.chart: Chart is explicitly an estimate/no-data display, which earns the estimate ceiling.
D.drilldown: Proposed calls are not executed and the breakdown is only a plan; some follow-ups work, but no traced breakdown layer is reported.
D.export: Template is explicitly labelled estimate and contains no data.
D.repro: Two numeric claims are untraced and planned calls have no reproducible result.
D.accuracy: Separates estimates from measurements and does not contradict the reference record.
D.limits: Acknowledges that no data was measured, but its proposed window is not the reference window and it misses the applicable source-record limits.
D.verdict: Gives a cautious decision and confidence, but the ungrounded prior that food inflation likely leads weakens support.
D.facets: Most requested facets remain unmeasured; the qualitative onion seasonality claim is only an estimate.

A: Claims c1 reports strict index partition reads and historical row floors, which are not present in the supplied reference record.
B: Reports shares as portions of combined articles although c1 does not establish unique-article deduplication.
States a 107.1% row-floor check absent from the supplied record.
Misdescribes the censored period: c1 sets the exclusive end at 2026-06-01 and warns that the newest included month, May 2026, may be incomplete.
Describes the chart as selected months and omits most available monthly points.
D: States as an estimate that food inflation very likely out-covers each commodity, but the reference actually measures this comparison; the estimate is unsupported by this deliverable’s evidence.

raw.verdict: A is the strongest decision aid: it compares all three terms on one traced window, gives a complete monthly series and reproducible ratios, and distinguishes media attention from price movement. B adds useful spike observations but has material window, coverage, and overlap errors; C and D are transparent about missing measurements but do not answer the comparison.
